d.partTitle: Climate, Soils and Relief of Africa
d.notions: Climatic zone, relief, plateau, basin, Rift Valley, fold mountains, volcanic mountains, ferrallitic and ferruginous soils.
d.focus: Climate, soils and relief of Africa.
d.competence: Learners are able to relate the climate and relief of a place in Africa to the activities that people practise there.
objectives: Describe the main climatic zones of Africa.
Describe the main relief features of Africa.
Describe the main soils of Africa.
recall: Africa lies between 37°N and 35°S, and the Equator crosses its middle.
It is a plateau continent, with Kilimanjaro as its highest point and the Nile as its longest river.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: the wettest and driest towns of Cameroon.
situation: Douala receives about 4,000 mm of rain per year, Garoua about 1,000 mm and Maroua about 800 mm. On the Adamawa plateau, the air is cooler than in Garoua.
Nadia wonders why the climate changes so much from one part of Cameroon, and of Africa, to another.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Nadia does not understand why the climate changes so much from one part of Africa to another.
Which town is the wettest and which is the driest?
Douala is the wettest, with about 4,000 mm. Maroua is the driest, with about 800 mm.
How can Nadia find the reasons for these differences?
She can compare the latitude, the distance from the sea and the altitude of each town on a map.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the climate, relief and soils of Africa, which influence where people live and what they do.

qa.q: Look at the map. What climate is found around the Equator, and what climate is found around the tropics?
qa.a: Around the Equator, the climate is equatorial: hot and wet all year. Around the tropics, there are hot deserts: the Sahara, the Kalahari and the Namib.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: What do you notice about the climatic zones north and south of the Equator?
qa.a: The climatic zones are repeated in the same order north and south of the Equator: equatorial, tropical, semi-arid, desert and Mediterranean.

qa.q: Nairobi is almost on the Equator, but it is cool. Why?
qa.a: Nairobi is at a high altitude, about 1,700 m. Temperatures fall as altitude increases.

sum.title: I. Climate
sum.intro: The climate of Africa is mostly hot, because most of Africa lies between the tropics. Its zones are repeated north and south of the Equator:
items: Around the Equator, it is hot and wet all year, as in the Congo Basin and southern Cameroon.
Between the equatorial zone and the deserts, there is a wet season and a dry season, as in Garoua.
Near the tropics, rainfall is low or very low, as in the Sahel, the Sahara, the Kalahari and the Namib.
The far north and far south have hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters. Highlands are cooler, as in Ethiopia and Kenya.

qa.q: Look at the relief map. Which part of Africa is higher: the north-west or the south-east?
qa.a: The south and east are higher. We speak of "High Africa" in the south and east, and "Low Africa" in the north and west.

qa.q: In East Africa, the land has sunk between two lines of faults, forming a long, deep valley with lakes. What is it called?
qa.a: It is called the Great Rift Valley. It runs from Ethiopia to Mozambique and contains lakes such as Tanganyika and Malawi.

qa.q: Mount Cameroon and Kilimanjaro were formed by volcanoes. Which mountains of Africa were formed by folding?
qa.a: The Atlas Mountains in the north-west and the Cape Ranges in the far south were formed by folding.

sum.title: II. Relief
sum.intro: The main relief features of Africa are the following:
items: Most of Africa is a plateau. High Africa lies in the south and east, and Low Africa in the north and west.
Large low basins lie inside the plateau: the Congo, Chad, Niger and Kalahari Basins.
Fold mountains: the Atlas and the Cape Ranges. Volcanic mountains: Kilimanjaro, Mount Kenya and Mount Cameroon.
The Great Rift Valley is a long, deep valley in East Africa, formed by faulting. It contains many lakes.

qa.q: Farmers on the slopes of Mount Cameroon grow bananas, cocoa and tea on very fertile soils. Where do these soils come from?
qa.a: These soils come from volcanic rocks. Volcanic soils are very fertile.

sum.title: III. Soils
sum.intro: The main soils of Africa are the following:
items: Red ferrallitic soils are found in the equatorial zone, and ferruginous soils in the savanna. They are leached and only fairly fertile.
Desert soils are sandy or stony, poor in humus and often salty.
Volcanic soils (Mount Cameroon, Ethiopia) and alluvial soils (Nile valley and delta) are very fertile.

evaluation: Why is the climate of Africa mostly hot?
It is mostly hot because most of Africa lies between the two tropics.
What is the Great Rift Valley?
The Great Rift Valley is a long, deep valley in East Africa, formed by faulting, with many lakes.
Name two types of very fertile soils in Africa.
Volcanic soils and alluvial soils are very fertile.
remediation: The climate that is hot and wet all year is the ______ climate.
The fold mountains of north-west Africa are the ______.
The long valley of East Africa formed by faulting is the Great ______ Valley.
The soils of Mount Cameroon are ______ soils.
The soils of the Nile valley are ______ soils.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. equatorial 2. altitude 3. Atlas 4. Rift 5. volcanic 6. alluvial
